corpus_checks.name: sensitive dictations produce no memory
corpus_checks.why: Health, money, relationships and other people's circumstances are refused in code, not by prompt.

corpus_checks.name: passing states produce no memory
corpus_checks.why: True now, misleading later. Recording moods would make every other memory less reliable.

corpus_checks.name: acknowledgements produce no memory
corpus_checks.why: "Okay" and "testing one two" are noise; keeping them would dilute retrieval.

corpus_checks.name: every memory is traceable to a dictation
corpus_checks.why: A memory with no provenance cannot be checked, corrected, or trusted.

corpus_checks.name: contradictions supersede rather than duplicate
corpus_checks.why: The old belief is history, not a mistake to delete. The user can see what changed.

corpus_checks.name: recogniser mis-spellings are learned
corpus_checks.detail: 8 names with at least one observed variant
corpus_checks.why: This is the only channel from semantic memory into ordinary dictation.

corpus_checks.name: repeated statements are reinforced, not duplicated
corpus_checks.detail: 24 memories with three or more mentions
corpus_checks.why: Repetition is the main evidence that something is worth acting on.

corpus_checks.name: every dictation has an episode
corpus_checks.why: Episodes are the retrieval floor: even when nothing was worth promoting, "what happened" stays answerable.
